subject.title: [Feature Request]: Native Prompt Caching Support for Amazon Nova (Bedrock)

question: Should OpenClaw treat Amazon Nova generation models as Bedrock prompt-cache eligible by default, while preserving the no-cache fallback for unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing provider cache eligibility affects auth/provider routing, request payload shape, cost behavior, and compatibility for existing Bedrock users, so maintainer product ownership should accept the direction before merge.

options.title: Accept Nova caching via provider policy
options.body: Review and land the linked PR or a narrow equivalent after live Bedrock Nova proof confirms cache points and opt-out behavior work.

options.title: Keep current no-cache default
options.body: Reject the direction and close both the issue and linked PR with a supported workaround such as AWS automatic prompt caching or an explicit force/debug path.

recommendation.title: Accept Nova caching via provider policy
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked PR or a narrow equivalent after live Bedrock Nova proof confirms cache points and opt-out behavior work.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main policy gates are currently blamed to this author and they cover the cross-file provider and agent decision surface.
